_about: Cross-industry blocker checklist used by the Blocker agent. Starter version: Juan owns the final wording. Each rule matches CPC prefixes; 'all' rules apply to every patent. burden is high, medium or low and feeds the Clear path component of the revival score.

rules.title: Follow-on and improvement patents
rules.check: Later patents that cite this one, especially from the same owner, may claim the improvements a product needs. Check which are still in force before building.
rules.where_to_look: Forward citations on the patent record; USPTO Patent Center for each candidate's status

rules.title: Live family members
rules.check: Continuations, divisionals and foreign counterparts can stay in force after one patent lapses. A live US continuation can block the same invention.
rules.where_to_look: Family and worldwide applications on the patent record

rules.title: Revival of the lapsed patent
rules.check: An owner can petition to accept a late maintenance fee and reinstate the patent. Risk is highest in the first 24 months after lapse.
rules.where_to_look: Legal events (reinstatement codes) on the patent record

rules.title: Trade secrets and know-how
rules.check: The patent discloses the invention, not necessarily the manufacturing know-how. Expect to rebuild process details yourself.
rules.where_to_look: Talk to the inventors or the original owner

rules.title: FDA drug or biologic approval and exclusivity
rules.check: A drug needs FDA approval (NDA or BLA) before sale. Regulatory exclusivity can block generics even after patents expire: 5 years for a new chemical entity, 3 years for new clinical studies, 7 years for orphan drugs, 12 years for biologics.
rules.where_to_look: FDA Orange Book (drugs) and Purple Book (biologics)

rules.title: FDA medical device clearance
rules.check: Most devices need 510(k) clearance, De Novo classification or PMA approval before sale. Class III devices need clinical data.
rules.where_to_look: FDA 510(k), De Novo and PMA databases; product classification database

rules.title: EPA pesticide registration and data exclusivity
rules.check: Pesticides and biocides need EPA registration under FIFRA. The original registrant's data has 10 years of exclusive use and 15 years of compensation rights.
rules.where_to_look: EPA Pesticide Product and Label System (PPLS)

rules.title: EPA new chemical review
rules.check: A new chemical substance needs a premanufacture notice under TSCA before commercial manufacture.

rules.title: Drinking water and discharge standards
rules.check: Products in contact with drinking water usually need NSF/ANSI 61 certification; discharge systems need EPA or state permits.
rules.where_to_look: NSF certified product listings; EPA NPDES

rules.title: Industry standards and standard-essential patents
rules.check: Wireless products must implement standards (3GPP, IEEE 802.11) that are covered by many other live standard-essential patents licensed on FRAND terms. Radios also need FCC equipment authorization.
rules.where_to_look: ETSI IPR database; FCC equipment authorization

rules.title: Battery safety and transport certification
rules.check: Lithium cells need UN 38.3 testing for shipping and usually UL or IEC safety certification for sale.
rules.where_to_look: UL and IEC standards (UL 1642, UL 2054, IEC 62133); PHMSA rules

rules.title: Grid interconnection and equipment certification
rules.check: Generation equipment needs IEC or UL certification and a utility interconnection agreement.
rules.where_to_look: IEC 61400 (wind), UL 1741 (inverters), the local utility's interconnection rules

rules.title: Dense live patents and open standards
rules.check: Software fields have many overlapping live patents; check recent filings by large incumbents. Data products may also face privacy rules (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA).
rules.where_to_look: Recent forward citations from large assignees

rules.title: Material and machine patents
rules.check: Printer hardware may be free while specific materials, powders or process parameters stay patented.

rules.title: Export controls and laser safety
rules.check: Some optics and lasers are export controlled (EAR Category 6). Laser products sold in the US must meet FDA CDRH laser performance standards.
